newsitem.title: CHAD: Chad formally bans weapons from schools.
newsitem.headline: Chad formally bans weapons from schools.

text.p: Chad's government has formally banned guns, knives and other weapons from schools where they have circulated freely since the days of the civil war and conflict with Libya in the 1980s.

Education Minister Nagoum Yamassoum told state radio on Tuesday that any student found with a weapon would be immediately expelled. The ban follows a knife attack on a headmaster in the northern town of Faya Largeau.
"The Chadian authorities are determined to end the disorder which has reigned since 1979," he said.
Government sources say that since 1979, when civil war erupted, students have often carried weapons at school, making it impossible for teachers to exercise proper control.
The headmaster was stabbed in the back 10 times. The reason for the attack, which he survived, was not immediately clear.
On the wider security front, Chadian security forces have summarily executed scores of criminals as part of a crackdown on violent crime.
Chad has been relatively stable since President Idriss Deby, a former northern guerrilla leader, seized power in 1990 in a French-backed coup.
Deby won a seven-year presidential term in July.

His supporters were expected to take a majority of seats in parliamentary elections due to end with a second round on February 23. Results from the January 5 first round were expected to be released on Wednesday.
